title: ～てごらん — gentle “try ～ing”
summary: Verb te-form + ごらん is a soft way to tell someone to try or look at something: “try ～ing.” It is used by a person speaking to a child or someone younger or closer, in a kind tone. It is not used toward superiors.

patterns.gloss: te-form + ごらん (読んでごらん, 見てごらん)

patterns.form: 動詞て形 ＋ ごらんなさい
patterns.gloss: te-form + ごらんなさい: fuller and a bit stronger form

body.p: ごらん comes from 御覧, the honorific “look” (a form of 見る). ～てごらん literally says “look at (how it goes) after doing ～.” That is why it carries the idea of trying something to see the result.
Parents, teachers, and elders use it to encourage a child or a friend: 食べてごらん (try eating it), 見てごらん (look!). A kind, encouraging tone is natural.
It is a mild command, not a request, so avoid it for superiors; use ～てみてください or ～てみませんか instead. The negative form is not used.

examples.ja: この本（ほん）を読（よ）んでごらん。
あそこの看板（かんばん）を見（み）てごらん、面白（おもしろ）い絵（え）があるよ。
examples.romaji: Asoko no kanban o mite goran, omoshiroi e ga aru yo.
examples.tr: Look at that sign over there; there's a funny picture.

examples.ja: 分（わ）からないなら、先生（せんせい）に聞（き）いてごらん。
examples.romaji: Wakaranai nara, sensei ni kiite goran.
examples.tr: If you don't understand, try asking the teacher.

pitfalls: Do not use it to a boss or teacher. It sounds like an order from above. Use ～てみてください.
The form is fixed: te-form + ごらん. Not ～ないでごらん.
